title: Variant compatibility harmonization checklist — tokenizer/context/tooling
creator: Avery Chen
description: We need a maintainable compatibility matrix that guarantees fallback model variants are safe to route to across regions and customer tiers. The matrix must capture tokenizer equivalence, context/KV cache behavior, and tooling (sampling/streaming/function-calling) parity so smart routing policies can make deterministic decisions. This ticket defines the harmonization checklist, required automation, test harnesses, and rollout plan to keep the matrix current as new variants and quantization families are onboarded.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical compatibility matrix (CSV + metadata) exists in the repo and is the single source of truth for routing decisions
Automated CI that validates tokenizer/tokenization equivalence and context-size compatibility for every new variant PR
KV/cache parity smoke tests that run in runtime unit/integration suites and surface regressions to the Console dashboard
Tooling behavior (streaming, functions/tool-calling, structured output) is annotated per-variant and used by the router to enforce soft/strict fallbacks
A documented maintenance process with owners, cadence (weekly), and emergency rollback playbook
tasks: Survey current matrix artifacts across repos and consolidate into sources/team/compatibility-matrix.csv
Define canonical schema for matrix rows (variant_id, tokenizer_family, tokenizer_version, max_context_tokens, kv_cache_behavior, streaming_supported, functions_support, quantization_profile)
Implement CI job (ci/compat-check) that runs tokenization diffs and context-growth smoke tests on variant PRs
Add KV cache parity harness that replays representative prefixes and validates cache hits/misses and generation alignment
Integrate compatibility metadata into the routing policy service so decision engine can consult soft/strict flags
Create Console dashboard tiles showing compatibility drift, last-validated timestamp, and failing variants by region/tier
Run a one-week canary where smart-router uses the matrix in region us-west-2 with 5% traffic and monitor fallbacks
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Routing, and DevEx. Agreed canonical schema and CSV approach (not a DB initially) to reduce rollout friction.
2026-03-06: Tokenization diff tool prototype (token-diff) implemented by @marco and validated on three variants; found off-by-one in variant v2-quantized-1 causing misaligned BOS tokenization.
2026-03-08: KV cache harness design doc uploaded to Confluence (link below). Took recommendation to compare cached-generation logits rather than tokens for noisy quantized families.
2026-03-11: CI job drafted in ci/compat-check; running token diffs now increases PR time ~18s. Decided to run full KV parity nightly rather than on every PR to limit CI cost.
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Kapoor): favor conservative fallbacks for P0 customer traffic — set strict fallback flag until variant passes KV parity
Design (Elena Morales): requested Console visualization mockups that show per-region variant compatibility heatmap
Security (Nina Patel): requested that any matrix artifact referencing model artifacts in private registries includes a pointer to access control docs
decisions: Use CSV+YAML sidecar for metadata as single source of truth to keep it git-native and auditable
Tokenization validation will be exact-match for stable families and distributional (statistical) checks for aggressive quantized families
Routing will interpret compatibility flags as: SKIP (do not route), SOFT (route only for non-critical tiers), STRICT (allowed for all tiers)
Full KV parity checks will run nightly and set a timestamp in the matrix; PR-level checks will validate tokenizer and max_context only
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: CI cost and timeouts as matrix grows. Mitigation: progressive validation (PR: cheap checks, nightly: expensive checks), and shard KV tests by variant families.
Risk: False positives from token-diff on languages with heavy tokenization ambiguity. Mitigation: language-aware thresholds and curated test prompts per language
Risk: Router coupling to matrix schema. Mitigation: add a thin compatibility service that exposes stable read APIs and enforces schema translation
next_steps: Finish CI job and land PR for canonical CSV schema (owner: Marco)
Wire compatibility service read API and add a caching layer for router queries (owner: Priya Singh)
Implement nightly KV parity runner and start seeding matrix timestamps (owner: SRE)
Schedule Console mock review with Design and Product to finalize visuals for compatibility heatmap
notes: Keep matrix human-readable — operators should be able to audit and fix entries via PRs
Consider future migration to a small metadata DB if read latency from CSV becomes a bottleneck
We should include a small set of reproducible test prompts per language and per domain (coding, chat, summarization)
